note: Closed-class English words of at least three letters (articles, determiners, prepositions and conjunctions) that refer to no one and are not a given name or a surname in any major naming culture, with one declared exception, "the", which is also a Vietnamese name part written without its diacritic (Thế) and which the rule below keeps wherever it is written as a name; where there was doubt a word was left out, because a word left out is only redacted where it need not be, while a word kept could let a name leave. The rule in exulanica/epistemics/saved_names.py: a part of a person's or a voice's saved name is not recognised alone when it is one of these words AND the saved name writes it in lowercase AND capitalises another part, as the "the" of a saved "Joe the Plumber" is written. The saved name's own writing says the word is not a name there: "Nguyen The Anh" keeps "The", and a saved name written all in lowercase keeps every part. The whole saved name is recognised either way. tests/test_saved_name_function_words.py holds this list against given names and surnames from many naming cultures.
